put.description: Despite the name, this is what actually starts the sync — it does not just close the session for bookkeeping. Call it once all products have been added with add_products_to_publish_session; it stops accepting further additions and schedules the session to be processed asynchronously. The session must currently be CREATED (i.e. not already closed, cancelled or finished). Poll get_publish_session for progress and get_publish_session_report once it reaches a terminal status.

post.description: Creates an empty session that acts as a container for one publish/unpublish run, scoped to the given contexts. It does not accept product ids or start syncing by itself: add products with add_products_to_publish_session, then call complete_publish_session (PUT /session/{id}/done) to start processing them. Fails if the organization already has too many sessions pending at once — finish or cancel older sessions before creating new ones.

post.description: Records the target publish state (PUBLISH or UNPUBLISH) for a batch of products in one context; it does not push anything live by itself. To actually publish or unpublish the products, create a session with create_publish_session, add the same product ids with add_products_to_publish_session, and start it with complete_publish_session. Product ids that do not resolve to an active product in this organization are silently ignored rather than causing a failure.

get.summary: Get products issues for the session.
get.description: Lists the individual products that failed or were skipped while syncing this session, grouped by issue type (e.g. version conflicts from a stale lastUpdate, or products that could not be published). Use it to explain a PUBLISHED_WITH_ISSUES result at the product level, once get_publish_session_report shows the session reached a terminal status. For asset- or entity-level failures use get_publish_session_asset_issues or get_publish_session_entity_issues instead.

get.description: Returns running totals for the session and can be called at any time, including while it is still IN_PROGRESS — counts simply reflect what has been processed so far. metrics/categoriesMetrics stay empty until the session starts pushing data for a context, and break the totals down per context. For the underlying per-product/asset/entity issues, use get_publish_session_product_issues, get_publish_session_asset_issues or get_publish_session_entity_issues instead.

get.description: Use this to poll a session's progress after closing it. A session moves through CREATED (open for adding products) -> INITIALIZED -> IN_PROGRESS -> a terminal status: PUBLISHED, PUBLISHED_WITH_ISSUES (finished, but see get_publish_session_report and the issue tools for what failed), CANCELLED, or FAILED. errorReports tracks the background generation of downloadable issue files and is unrelated to the summary counts returned by get_publish_session_report.
